## What the ticket said

refreshCollab(pack, {pull:true}) is how a scene ARRIVES in a room, and its pull sat BELOW the `seq !== collab.seq` guard. onSceneSelected fires it un-awaited, so any caller that bumps collab.seq in the window between the info read and the pull abandoned the arrival pull with no retry and no error — and every superseding refresh passes pull:false, so it fetches nothing. The person who just opened a collab scene sees an empty room for up to the 60s poll.

Objective: say in refreshCollab what BAD-090 said in runCollabSync — supersession cancels the PAINT, not the TRANSFER.

SCOPE WAS NARROWED MID-TICKET by Eric: the WEB client only. renderer/app.js is deliberately left with the old (buggy) shape; its identical fix is recorded on BAD-041, the ticket that splits that 9k-line file. Deliverables are exactly web/collabweb-model.js and test/collabreads.test.js. Vitelotte touching renderer/app.js would be a defect — confirm the working tree shows only those two files modified.

The ticket demanded three things be decided AND written down in the code:

1. Which conditions still cancel the pull. Scene identity must; collab.seq must not. `collab.offline` and `collabActive()` are read before the pull today — say what they mean once the pull moves above the guard.
2. What the superseded call returns and what it must NOT leave behind. A superseded refresh still returns false, and must not toast, must not overwrite collab.remote/collab.resolved, must not repaint or re-arm the poll on top of a newer call's state. The pull's WRITES go to the take store and are wanted whoever asked for them; the paint is the part that belongs to the current call only.
3. Whether moving the pull above the guard changes the wire order BAD-090 pinned. It must not: the read stays at the tail of the sync cycle and before the first download-url. If the change moves a read, BAD-090's invariant is broken and the answer is a different fix, not a relaxed test.

BAD-090's outcome, verbatim from the ledger, for the invariant you are protecting: "A full sync cycle is now upload-url, commit, info, download-url — one info where there were two ... the pull decides from the snapshot its CALLER just took, not from whatever is lying around, because a stale snapshot delays a push but loses a pull a cycle; the read stays at the tail, since a front-loaded one would put info-upload-url-PUT-commit back on the wire, byte for byte what BAD-080 deleted; and the pull stays in runCollabSync rather than riding refreshCollab's pull branch, which is the obvious fold and sits under a collab.seq supersession guard that is right for a paint and wrong for a transfer. That third was the first cut, blocked by the reviewer Katahdin spawned and now pinned. The naive fold was built and run against the same tests: it reaches one read and fails four assertions, so a count-only test would have passed the regression." Read /Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud/ledger/tickets/BAD-090.md in full.

## What the cut actually did — check every claim of this

refreshCollab's body is now three parts with three different guards:

- ABSORB — collab.info, skewMs, hbPhase. Written by whichever read landed LAST, gated by a NEW `collab.readSeq` field, and deliberately ABOVE the seq check, because pullTakes decides from collab.info and a pull left without one opens its own bootstrap `info` — the second read BAD-090 deleted.
- PAINT — loading, the renders, collab.remote/collab.resolved, the toast, startCollabPolling. Gated on `mine()` (seq === collab.seq).
- TRANSFER — the pull, gated on `here()` (scene identity) and nothing else.

Two helpers `here()`/`mine()` are declared ABOVE the read so the span between the read and the pull names no sequence at all; a new structural test greps for exactly that.

One judgement call to attack hardest: a superseded call whose pull actually brought takes down DOES run the transfer's tail — collab.remote = listRemoteTakes, resolveCollabTakes, renderCollabModal/renderBoothCollab — which is literally "overwrite collab.remote/collab.resolved and repaint", which item 2 of the brief forbade. The reasoning was: the superseding refresh passes pull:false and its own tail runs long before the superseded pull's downloads finish, so without this the takes land on disk and the room STILL looks empty — the exact symptom the ticket exists to fix; and runCollabSync's own post-pull tail does exactly these three lines guarded on scene identity alone, so this matches BAD-090's reference shape. It does NOT toast, does NOT re-arm the poll, does NOT touch collab.loading, and returns false. Decide whether that is right, whether it is safe against a newer call that has moved to a different room or dropped the pin, and whether the comment explains it well enough for the next person to not undo it.
